public_sources.title: Game-Theoretic Statistics and Safe Anytime-Valid Inference
public_sources.relevance: General primary/reference framework for conditional e-variables/e-processes and confidence sequences used to distinguish predictable conditional bounds from ordinary fixed-sample calibration.

public_sources.title: Estimating means of bounded random variables by betting
public_sources.relevance: Primary source for nonasymptotic/time-uniform bounded-mean confidence sequences; used as a candidate tool for ongoing mismatch monitoring, not as proof that a finite conformance sample bounds future conditional mismatch under distribution shift.

public_sources.title: Batch Invariance - vLLM
public_sources.relevance: Current official evidence that deterministic execution is an explicit runtime mode with a bounded supported domain and performance tradeoff, strengthening the preference for contract-based identity over purely statistical mismatch certification.

public_sources.title: LLM-42: Enabling Determinism in LLM Inference with Verified Speculation
public_sources.relevance: Primary system showing a per-request verify/rollback path can enforce determinism selectively, offering an operational alternative to inferring identity from rare observed mismatches.

approximate_identity_bound.setup: Let X_t be the canonical logical paired sign with H0: P(X_t=+ | past)<=1/2. Let Y_t be the sign returned by fastest physical replica. Suppose a predictable/runtime-certified bound P(Y_t != X_t | past)<=epsilon_t is valid before seeing Y_t.
approximate_identity_bound.selected_null: By coupling, P(Y_t=+ | past)<=1/2+epsilon_t. Therefore the original +1.5/-0.5 factor is no longer valid when epsilon_t>0 because its conditional expectation can reach 1+epsilon_t.
approximate_identity_bound.robust_factor: Set p0_t=1/2+epsilon_t. For any predictable r_t>p0_t, use e_t(+)=r_t/p0_t and e_t(-)=(1-r_t)/(1-p0_t). Its conditional expectation is <=1 for every selected-sign probability p<=p0_t, so the product remains an e-process under this approximate-identity null.
approximate_identity_bound.alternative_separation: If the canonical good alternative is P(X_t=+|past)>=1/2+Delta and the same mismatch bound applies adversarially, then P(Y_t=+|past)>=1/2+Delta-epsilon_t. The worst-case observable gap is Delta-2epsilon_t. Uniform separation therefore requires epsilon_t<Delta/2.
approximate_identity_bound.example: For canonical q=0.60 (Delta=.10), an adversarial identity-error bound of 5% eliminates the worst-case gap entirely. Approximate identity can be statistically tolerated, but mismatch must be materially smaller than the effect size one hopes to certify.

finite_horizon_power_tax.model: 50 logical signs, commit threshold 1/alpha_test, alpha_global=.05, independent calibration failure budget delta=.005, alpha_test=.045, robust likelihood-ratio-style factor using r=.75 and p0=.5+epsilon. Canonical good q=.60; worst selected good probability q-epsilon.
finite_horizon_power_tax.interpretation: The robust factor prevents Type-I inflation when a valid predictable epsilon bound exists, but even small mismatch materially taxes short-horizon power. These numbers are exact finite-state calculations for this factor/horizon, not a claim of optimal betting.

conformance_sample_calibration.fixed_disjoint_iid_model: If a predeclared disjoint conformance sample contains n independent replica groups from the same stationary certified domain and observes zero mismatches, the one-sided exact 1-delta upper bound is epsilon_U=1-delta^(1/n). This is a fixed-sample statement.
conformance_sample_calibration.risk_accounting: If the conformance upper bound fails with probability at most delta and the fresh evaluation test is run at alpha_test, then a simple union bound gives overall false-commit probability <=delta+alpha_test. Thus calibration confidence consumes explicit global risk budget unless a joint e-process construction is used.
conformance_sample_calibration.critical_limitation: A marginal iid mismatch-rate bound from conformance does not by itself imply the per-attempt conditional bound P(Y_t!=X_t|past)<=epsilon required by the robust e-factor under adaptive/nonstationary serving. Fingerprint drift, prompt strata, load, batch size and hardware placement can concentrate mismatches. Prefer a deterministic runtime contract or stratified/predictable bounds; use time-uniform mismatch monitoring only as evidence within stated stationarity/conditional assumptions.

audit_level_coupling_fallback.statement: If no conditional epsilon bound is available but each of N canonical-vs-selected logical groups has marginal mismatch probability <=epsilon, couple the selected sign vector to the canonical vector. Any false-commit event differs from the canonical process only if at least one group mismatches, so FWER_selected <= FWER_canonical + P(any mismatch) <= FWER_canonical + N*epsilon by union bound.
audit_level_coupling_fallback.current_50_pair_example: The exact canonical null crossing probability for the current 50-pair +1.5/-0.5 process is 0.0375904302. To keep the crude bound <=.05 using N=50 requires epsilon <= (0.05-0.0375904302)/50 = 0.00024819 per logical group.
audit_level_coupling_fallback.certification_cost: With zero mismatches and a 95% one-sided fixed-sample binomial bound, proving epsilon_U<0.00024819 under iid conformance would require about 12,069 groups. This makes rare-mismatch coupling a poor primary certification path compared with deterministic runtime guarantees or a valid conditional robust factor.
audit_level_coupling_fallback.scope: The N*epsilon bound is deliberately crude but does not require mismatch independence across deployment groups; it does require valid per-group marginal bounds in the deployment domain.

determinism_gate_recommendation.tier_0: No deterministic contract / default stochastic serving: independent hedges are distinct attempts; never fastest-select for single-attempt quality inference.
determinism_gate_recommendation.tier_1: Finite conformance only: use for monitoring/engineering confidence, not as a claim of epsilon=0. If a statistical epsilon bound is used, state iid/stationarity/stratification assumptions and charge calibration failure probability to the error budget.
determinism_gate_recommendation.tier_2: Runtime deterministic contract within a frozen fingerprint (batch-invariant/fixed-shape/verified deterministic path, supported model/hardware, deterministic sampler/random tape): first-completion physical replication can be treated as identity-preserving inside that certified domain, with ongoing mismatch/fingerprint alarms.
determinism_gate_recommendation.tier_3: Any observed logical mismatch or fingerprint drift immediately demotes the affected class; fastest selection is disabled/fail-closed until recertification.

new_measurement_validity_rules: A nonzero replica mismatch rate need not make hedging impossible, but it changes the null. If a predictable conditional mismatch bound epsilon is valid, test fastest-selected signs against p0=.5+epsilon rather than .5.

For a target effect margin Delta, approximate identity has worst-case separation Delta-2epsilon. Require epsilon materially below Delta/2; do not certify tiny improvements with a replica equivalence error of comparable size.

Do not convert a zero-mismatch conformance sample into a deterministic guarantee. Separate runtime-contract evidence, fixed-sample mismatch bounds, time-uniform monitoring and deployment distribution assumptions.
When calibration consumes risk, account for it explicitly in lifetime/global false-commit budget instead of reporting only the downstream test alpha.

If only an audit-level mismatch bound is defensible, the naive union-coupling requirement can be extremely strict; this is evidence that operational determinism should be proven by construction where possible, not inferred from rare failures alone.
scope_guards: The robust-factor derivation assumes a predictable conditional upper bound on selected-vs-canonical mismatch; a marginal mismatch frequency is insufficient under arbitrary adaptive serving.

The conformance sample-size table assumes independent fixed-sample Bernoulli mismatches and zero observed failures. Other counts require the full exact interval; optional stopping requires an anytime-valid confidence sequence/e-process.
The q=.60 power table uses one chosen betting alternative r=.75 and N=50; it is not a minimax or horizon-optimal design.
A deterministic runtime's own correctness guarantee can be narrower or stronger than statistical conformance; every guarantee must be scoped to the exact model/hardware/version/configuration domain.

frontier.action: Construct a joint online monitor for deterministic fingerprint and replica mismatch using a Bernoulli e-process/confidence sequence, but keep fastest-selection admission tied to a runtime deterministic contract or a genuinely predictable epsilon bound; quantify demotion thresholds and false-alarm budget.

Optimize the approximate-identity e-factor for finite horizons under uncertainty in epsilon and effect Delta; compare fixed r=.75, mixture and Bellman policies while preserving p0=.5+epsilon validity.
Develop stratified mismatch certification by prompt family, model, batch/concurrency and hardware placement so an observed aggregate zero-mismatch rate cannot hide a high-risk serving stratum.

Compare deterministic-by-construction systems (batch invariance, fixed-shape scheduling, verify-rollback) on the same logical-attempt contract and measure whether their determinism tax is lower than the statistical power/sample-size tax of approximate identity.

frontier.exact_next_action: Derive an anytime-valid mismatch monitor and finite-horizon robust betting policy for p0=.5+epsilon, then stress it under fingerprint-stratified mismatch bursts to test whether marginal conformance can mask conditional invalidity.
